claim_scope: Deterministic activation, observation, containment, and stated recovery for the enumerated public behavioral RTL sites only.

iverilog_suppressions.scope: Icarus elaboration diagnostic for IEEE always-@* dynamic array sensitivity
iverilog_suppressions.rationale: The entire array is intentionally in the combinational sensitivity set; simulation behavior is required and cross-checked by Verilator.

verilator_suppressions.rationale: Bench stimulus variables use declaration initialization and procedural assignment.
Directed benches expose diagnostic pins that are intentionally not sampled at every site.
Reduced harness instances intentionally leave unrelated observation-only pins open.

sites.expected_observation: Corrupt route-record CRC sets poison and the sticky CRC diagnostic.
sites.containment: The decoded mask cannot be consumed as an unpoisoned context.
sites.recovery: Discard the poisoned context; a later legal record remains independently decodable.

sites.expected_observation: An expert ID outside the configured population sets bad-field, poison, and no enable bit.
sites.containment: No out-of-range wordline or expert enable is asserted.
sites.recovery: Discard the record and accept a subsequent legal record after normal queue drain.

sites.expected_observation: A repeated expert ID is reported in the duplicate-slot bitmap while the first occurrence is retained.
sites.containment: Only one wordline enable is produced for the repeated expert.
sites.recovery: The deduplicated legal route proceeds without transaction poison.

sites.expected_observation: A nonzero reserved field sets bad-field and poisons the context.
sites.containment: Reserved encodings cannot alter the decoded service mask silently.
sites.recovery: Discard the poisoned record; later legal records are unaffected.

sites.expected_observation: An illegal top-k count is classified as bad-field and poisoned.
sites.containment: No service launch is authorized from the malformed count.
sites.recovery: Discard the record and continue with a legal route record.

sites.expected_observation: A single-bit injected event returns the original architectural word with correctable syndrome and no poison.
sites.containment: Corrupt injected data is never exposed at the architectural response.
sites.recovery: Consume corrected data and record/scrub through the external macro policy.

sites.expected_observation: A representative multi-bit injection returns an uncorrectable syndrome with poison.
sites.containment: The affected read is prevented from committing as valid data.
sites.recovery: Abort/poison the owning transaction; macro repair or quarantine is an external gate.

sites.expected_observation: A legal logical-to-spare remap returns the spare-row word without poison.
sites.containment: The defective logical row is bypassed without changing logical content semantics.
sites.recovery: Continue service using the frozen repair map.

sites.expected_observation: A repair target outside physical depth produces a poisoned response.
sites.containment: No out-of-range physical array access can become architectural data.
sites.recovery: Reject the repair/read; load a valid quiescent repair map before service.

sites.expected_observation: An out-of-range logical address returns zero data with poison.
sites.containment: No physical word is aliased into the illegal logical address.
sites.recovery: Abort the request; valid later addresses remain usable.

sites.expected_observation: A response CRC error completes the matching tag with integrity error and poison.
sites.containment: Only the matching tag/session is terminated and its outstanding reservation is released.
sites.recovery: Retry or abort by policy; unrelated tags remain serviceable.

sites.expected_observation: A legal response after a prior CRC failure completes cleanly for its own session.
sites.containment: Historical sticky protocol evidence does not poison a later unrelated tag.
sites.recovery: Continue normal service on the healthy tag/channel.

sites.expected_observation: A response for an inactive/unallocated tag is reported as a poisoned protocol completion.
sites.containment: No active request reservation or session state is consumed by the unexpected response.
sites.recovery: Drop the response, retain active tags, and escalate repeated channel protocol faults.

sites.expected_observation: A terminal beat before the declared count poisons the same completion and sets protocol error.
sites.containment: Partial burst data cannot commit as a successful request.
sites.recovery: Release the tag and retry/abort the owning transaction.

sites.expected_observation: A missing terminal marker at the declared final beat poisons the same completion and sets protocol error.
sites.containment: The overlong burst cannot overwrite or remain attached to the completed tag.
sites.recovery: Release the tag and retry/abort; a late extra beat is treated as unexpected.

sites.expected_observation: A nonzero vendor-normalized response status is returned on the matching poisoned completion.
sites.containment: The error is contained to the owning tag/session with no successful commit.
sites.recovery: Apply corrected/retry/abort/channel-recovery policy for the classified status.

sites.expected_observation: The all-ones 16-bit minus-one encoding reserves exactly 65,536 beats in a 17-bit internal count.
sites.containment: The architectural maximum cannot wrap to zero and terminate or recycle the tag prematurely.
sites.recovery: Complete or explicitly abort the full request under the normal tag lifecycle.

sites.expected_observation: A different-tag admission concurrent with a terminal response preserves one outstanding reservation and both completions retain their sessions.
sites.containment: Neither the increment nor decrement is lost, and tag ownership cannot underflow, leak, or cross sessions.
sites.recovery: The newly admitted tag completes normally and returns the outstanding count to zero.

sites.expected_observation: A bad flit CRC produces one negative acknowledgement, protocol error, and no delivery.
sites.containment: No corrupt flit escapes the complete-packet receive buffer.
sites.recovery: Sender retries the retained packet or aborts after the retry limit.

sites.expected_observation: A bad terminal packet CRC produces one negative acknowledgement and no delivery.
sites.containment: No packet with inconsistent accumulated CRC reaches the service plane.
sites.recovery: Sender retries the complete retained packet.

sites.expected_observation: A later corrupt flit rejects the packet without exposing its earlier valid flit.
sites.containment: Complete-packet buffering prevents partial architectural delivery.
sites.recovery: Discard the receive buffer and accept a clean retry.

sites.expected_observation: A valid packet is delivered once and positively acknowledged without poison.
sites.containment: Delivery and acknowledgement refer to the same complete packet sequence.
sites.recovery: Advance the expected sequence and continue.

sites.expected_observation: A replay of the last accepted sequence is positively acknowledged but not redelivered.
sites.containment: Idempotence prevents duplicate state commit.
sites.recovery: Sender treats the acknowledgement as terminal and advances.

sites.expected_observation: An unexpected first-flit sequence is negatively acknowledged with no delivery.
sites.containment: The out-of-order packet cannot alter service state.
sites.recovery: Discard and retry the required sequence or abort.

sites.expected_observation: A packet whose flits carry different sequence IDs is negatively acknowledged with no delivery.
sites.containment: All flits in the receive buffer remain uncommitted.
sites.recovery: Discard the mixed packet and accept a clean retransmission.

sites.expected_observation: A legal packet following rejected sequence traffic is delivered and acknowledged once.
sites.containment: Prior CRC/sequence state does not contaminate the new packet.
sites.recovery: Advance expected sequence and resume service.

sites.expected_observation: A matching negative acknowledgement causes exactly one complete-packet retransmission and increments retry count.
sites.containment: The sender retains packet bits and sequence until terminal acknowledgement.
sites.recovery: Await a positive acknowledgement or exhaust the bounded retry policy.

sites.expected_observation: The original packet consumes one remote packet credit and its retry consumes none.
sites.containment: Retries cannot leak receive-buffer credits.
sites.recovery: Credit is returned only by the endpoint-level completion policy.

sites.expected_observation: Acknowledgement timeout emits a timeout indication and retransmits once.
sites.containment: The retained packet is replayed without a second credit debit or partial replacement.
sites.recovery: Accept a later matching ACK or terminally abort at the retry bound.

sites.expected_observation: A further NAK after the allowed retry sets terminal error, preserves retry diagnostics, and clears busy.
sites.containment: No additional unbounded transmission or successful completion occurs.
sites.recovery: Abort/poison the transaction and requalify the link before reuse if policy requires.

sites.expected_observation: An acknowledgement for another sequence is ignored while the sender remains busy.
sites.containment: The wrong ACK cannot retire or mutate the retained packet.
sites.recovery: Continue waiting for the matching ACK or timeout.

sites.expected_observation: A packet cannot be accepted when no remote complete-packet credit is available.
sites.containment: No packet state or credit counter changes without admission.
sites.recovery: Retry admission after credit is advertised.

sites.expected_observation: Host/control abort while waiting for ACK terminates the sender with error and no busy state.
sites.containment: The packet cannot later complete successfully from a stale ACK.
sites.recovery: Poison/abort owning state and start a new packet only after abort deasserts.

sites.expected_observation: A correctable event increments its saturating counter and captures first error without transaction poison or SAFE.
sites.containment: The active transaction remains usable because the event is classified correctable.
sites.recovery: Continue with corrected data and service policy.

sites.expected_observation: Telemetry fields and CRC16 reproduce the injected source, severity, epoch, transaction, and syndrome.
sites.containment: Diagnostic evidence is bound to one lossless record.
sites.recovery: Drain/acknowledge the record through the telemetry interface.

sites.expected_observation: An uncorrectable event increments its counter and poisons the active transaction without forcing global SAFE.
sites.containment: No successful commit is allowed for the affected transaction.
sites.recovery: Abort the affected transaction while unrelated service may continue.

sites.expected_observation: A later event does not overwrite the captured first-error severity, source, or transaction.
sites.containment: Root-cause evidence survives subsequent faults.
sites.recovery: Software explicitly clears first-error state after collection.

sites.expected_observation: The explicit clear operation removes first-error valid state.
sites.containment: Only the defined clear control can release the sticky record.
sites.recovery: The next event becomes the new first error.

sites.expected_observation: Transaction poison clears at an idle transaction boundary while sticky diagnostic history remains separate.
sites.containment: Poison cannot leak into an unrelated later transaction.
sites.recovery: Admit a new clean transaction after the boundary.

sites.expected_observation: A fatal event increments the fatal counter, poisons active work, asserts SAFE request, and blocks admission immediately.
sites.containment: No one-cycle post-fatal admission leak or successful affected commit is allowed.
sites.recovery: Drain/isolate and require explicit platform requalification.

sites.expected_observation: An asserted upstream poison input becomes monotonic poison for the active transaction.
sites.containment: Downstream logic cannot silently clear the propagated error during the transaction.
sites.recovery: Clear only at the idle transaction boundary after abort/retire.

sites.expected_observation: A counter at all ones remains saturated after another matching event.
sites.containment: Diagnostic counts never wrap to a misleading low value.
sites.recovery: Retain saturation indication and service according to policy.

sites.expected_observation: Admission blocks at the reserved-entry threshold while queued telemetry remains valid.
sites.containment: Capacity is preserved for a terminal/fatal event instead of being consumed by new work.
sites.recovery: Drain telemetry below threshold before reopening admission.

sites.expected_observation: The reserved fatal event fills the queue and asserts SAFE/admission block.
sites.containment: Lossless terminal evidence is retained and no further work is admitted.
sites.recovery: Drain records under SAFE control and requalify.

sites.expected_observation: Watchdog expiry asserts timeout, SAFE request, and admission block in the expiry cycle.
sites.containment: Hung work cannot admit successors or remain silently active.
sites.recovery: Abort/drain and require watchdog/platform recovery.

sites.expected_observation: A complete legal BIST run returns pass, a nonzero signature, done state, and releases ownership.
sites.containment: Functional service cannot overlap BIST ownership.
sites.recovery: Publish the pass signature and return the resource to service.

sites.expected_observation: A data mismatch returns fail and captures the first reduced-test failing address.
sites.containment: The tested resource remains owned until the failure result is finalized.
sites.recovery: Repair/quarantine and rerun BIST before service.

sites.expected_observation: The explicit BIST injection hook forces a failing result without timeout.
sites.containment: The failure cannot be reported as a passing signature.
sites.recovery: Use the injected result to qualify the diagnostic path; clear before real BIST.

sites.expected_observation: Abort terminates a running BIST as non-pass, non-timeout, and releases busy ownership.
sites.containment: No partial test is promoted to a pass.
sites.recovery: Restart a complete test before enabling the resource.

sites.expected_observation: Start is ignored while the resource is unavailable; busy, done, and test ownership remain deasserted.
sites.containment: BIST cannot contend with active functional ownership.
sites.recovery: Quiesce the resource and issue a new start.

sites.expected_observation: A deliberately short timeout returns done, timeout, fail, and no busy state.
sites.containment: A hung macro/test callback cannot hold ownership indefinitely or report pass.
sites.recovery: Quarantine or reset the resource and rerun diagnostics.

sites.expected_observation: Reset functional state exposes the configured IDCODE and legal BYPASS without entering test mode.
sites.containment: Identity/bypass access does not isolate live service by itself.
sites.recovery: Continue functional operation or request controlled test entry.

sites.expected_observation: A test request during active service receives no grant, no test mode, and no isolation.
sites.containment: Test clocks/scan cannot seize a nonquiescent service resource.
sites.recovery: Quiesce service before reissuing the request.

sites.expected_observation: After quiescence, the armed request grants test mode and asserts service isolation.
sites.containment: Functional traffic is blocked before test controls become active.
sites.recovery: Complete diagnostics and follow the controlled exit sequence.

sites.expected_observation: Scan enable is asserted only with test grant and functional isolation.
sites.containment: Shift/capture activity cannot reach an unisolated service interface.
sites.recovery: Drop scan request before exiting test mode.

sites.expected_observation: A BIST request in granted test mode emits the bounded BIST start pulse.
sites.containment: BIST start cannot occur in functional ownership.
sites.recovery: Hold isolation until BIST completion.

sites.expected_observation: Test grant and isolation remain asserted while BIST reports busy even after requests drop.
sites.containment: Functional service cannot race a still-running BIST.
sites.recovery: Release test mode only after BIST done and not busy.

sites.expected_observation: After BIST completion and request release, test mode, grant, and isolation deassert.
sites.containment: No stale test ownership remains after the controlled exit.
sites.recovery: Requalify and return the resource to functional service.

sites.expected_observation: Service becoming active while test entry is armed cancels grant and test mode.
sites.containment: A quiescence race fails closed to functional ownership without mixed mode.
sites.recovery: Quiesce again and issue a fresh test request.

sites.expected_observation: Qualified reset/power inputs reach standby with core reset released but service disabled.
sites.containment: Inference cannot begin before explicit service request and qualification.
sites.recovery: Request service only after boot diagnostics complete.

sites.expected_observation: A legal service request enters active service with isolation removed.
sites.containment: Service enable is coupled to the legal state and qualified supplies/clocks.
sites.recovery: Continue service until throttle, quiesce, or fault.

sites.expected_observation: Thermal warning enters throttled state while preserving qualified service.
sites.containment: The response reduces service without corrupting protocol state.
sites.recovery: Return to active state after the warning clears.

sites.expected_observation: Clearing thermal warning removes throttle and restores active service.
sites.containment: Recovery does not bypass qualification or isolation guards.
sites.recovery: Continue at the unthrottled operating point.

sites.expected_observation: Asserting test enable during service forces SAFE, isolation, service disable, and a classified reset cause.
sites.containment: Functional and test modes cannot overlap.
sites.recovery: Drop service/test requests and execute explicit requalification.

sites.expected_observation: Explicit requalification after the interlock returns to standby and clears SAFE.
sites.containment: Service remains disabled until separately requested.
sites.recovery: Rerun required diagnostics, then request service.

sites.expected_observation: Fatal thermal input enters SAFE, records the thermal cause, and asserts core reset.
sites.containment: No new or continuing functional service is exposed through the fatal condition.
sites.recovery: Cool/isolate, diagnose, and explicitly requalify.

sites.expected_observation: Clock qualification loss enters SAFE, records the clock cause, and asserts core reset.
sites.containment: State cannot continue under an unqualified clock.
sites.recovery: Restore/qualify the clock and explicitly requalify.

sites.expected_observation: Once the core reports quiescent, the controller acknowledges quiesce, returns to standby, and disables service.
sites.containment: No new work enters while the state drains.
sites.recovery: Remove quiesce or power-transition according to policy.

sites.expected_observation: Commit of an incompletely loaded schedule bank is rejected without valid activation.
sites.containment: A partial schedule never reaches the service datapath.
sites.recovery: Finish all required entries and recommit.

sites.expected_observation: A slot encoding an illegal source produces an error and no commit-pending state.
sites.containment: No invalid route source can become active.
sites.recovery: Correct the shadow entry and rerun schedule validation.

sites.expected_observation: A schedule commit with bad manifest identity is rejected without activation.
sites.containment: Schedule data cannot be paired with the wrong image/manifest.
sites.recovery: Supply the matching identity and recommit.

sites.expected_observation: A valid commit remains pending while traffic is not quiescent and no epoch changes.
sites.containment: The active bank cannot change under in-flight traffic.
sites.recovery: Reach quiescent epoch boundary to activate atomically.

sites.expected_observation: At the legal boundary, commit acknowledges, publishes the requested ID, marks valid, and increments epoch.
sites.containment: All consumers observe one coherent bank/identity/epoch transition.
sites.recovery: Use the new bank for subsequent admitted work.

sites.expected_observation: An active legal slot exposes the validated source and expected-valid metadata.
sites.containment: Only the committed bank drives service selection.
sites.recovery: Advance through the deterministic schedule.

sites.expected_observation: A legal configure allocates the session, returns success/hit, and assigns a nonzero generation.
sites.containment: The entry is uniquely owned by its session and generation.
sites.recovery: Proceed to ordered lookup/retire operations.

sites.expected_observation: A duplicate configure of an existing session is rejected as busy.
sites.containment: The original session allocation is not overwritten.
sites.recovery: Use the existing session or free it before reconfiguration.

sites.expected_observation: Configuration beyond table capacity returns capacity error without corrupting busy state or integrity.
sites.containment: No existing session is evicted or aliased silently.
sites.recovery: Free capacity or reject admission upstream.

sites.expected_observation: Lookup with the wrong epoch returns epoch error and does not set busy.
sites.containment: Stale work cannot attach to current session state.
sites.recovery: Issue work with the active epoch or reconfigure.

sites.expected_observation: A legal lookup succeeds, hits the expected entry, and marks it busy.
sites.containment: One transaction owns the session mutation window.
sites.recovery: Retire or abort with the matching transaction.

sites.expected_observation: A nonmatching retire/operation returns an epoch/transaction error and preserves current position/busy ownership.
sites.containment: Late traffic cannot mutate the current owner.
sites.recovery: Discard the stale operation and complete the matching transaction.

sites.expected_observation: Matching abort records session poison, succeeds, and releases busy ownership.
sites.containment: Failed work cannot advance position or remain busy.
sites.recovery: Future lookup observes poison until explicit session free/reconfigure policy.

sites.expected_observation: A later legal lookup reports the sticky session poison state.
sites.containment: Downstream control cannot mistake a poisoned session for clean state.
sites.recovery: Abort/free the poisoned session before reuse.

sites.expected_observation: After free and reallocation, the entry receives a generation different from its earlier owner.
sites.containment: Late traffic from the prior allocation cannot match the reused slot.
sites.recovery: Use the new generation in all downstream ownership records.

sites.expected_observation: Post-lookup credit denial produces no-credit completion through session abort, with no service start/commit and with cleanup.
sites.containment: The busy session and any partial reservation cannot leak or retire successfully.
sites.recovery: Release cleanup ownership and allow a later command after terminal response.

sites.expected_observation: Service error returns internal status/source/syndrome, poison, session abort, no commit, and credit release.
sites.containment: No failed service result can reach the commit path or leave reserved capacity.
sites.recovery: Complete poisoned terminal cleanup; unrelated sessions remain serviceable.

sites.expected_observation: Stage watchdog produces timeout completion, poison, session abort, no commit, and credit release.
sites.containment: Hung service cannot retain session/credit ownership or commit later.
sites.recovery: Abort the transaction and requalify the failing service path.

sites.expected_observation: Matching host abort produces aborted completion, poison, session abort, no commit, and credit release.
sites.containment: No post-abort service completion can commit architectural state.
sites.recovery: Finish common abort cleanup and admit new work after terminal response.

external_gates.scope: Foundry ROM/SRAM ECC implementation, sense margin, retention, coupling, aging, and repair qualification.
HBM controller/PHY vendor behavior, lane repair, calibration, analog timing, and macro ECC qualification.
Stage-link SerDes/PHY BER, equalization, clock recovery, lane repair, and package channel behavior.
Target scan insertion, compression, stuck-at/transition ATPG coverage, diagnosis, and tester correlation.
Delay, bridging, open, crosstalk, power-integrity, thermal, radiation, and physical-layout fault coverage.
Target PDK timing/power/noise/reliability models and commercial signoff-tool qualification.
Defect density, yield, wafer probe, burn-in, repair exhaustion, package test, and production quality limits.
Target numerical-format qualification and end-to-end model quality under production workloads.
